title: FIAP X Video Processor
description: Uploads, processing, notifications and runtime of the api, worker and notifier (docs/observability.md).

panels.title: Videos uploaded
panels.description: Videos accepted by POST /api/v1/videos in the selected time range (RF2): videoproc_upload_bytes_count, one per accepted file.

panels.title: Videos DONE
panels.description: Jobs that ended DONE in the selected time range (RF1): frames extracted and the zip is downloadable.

panels.title: Videos FAILED
panels.description: Jobs whose video ended FAILED in the selected time range: bad content (failed) plus jobs given up after every retry (dead_lettered). Each one triggers a failure e-mail (RF5).

panels.title: Jobs in progress
panels.description: Videos being processed right now, summed over every worker replica (at most replicas x WORKER_CONCURRENCY).

panels.title: Jobs waiting
panels.description: Jobs waiting for a worker (ready messages in video.process). Grows during a burst of uploads and drains as workers finish: nothing is lost (RF2).

panels.title: DLQ depth
panels.description: Messages in video.process.dlq and video.notify.dlq: jobs or e-mails given up on. Should be 0; alerts VideoProcessDLQNotEmpty / VideoNotifyDLQNotEmpty.

panels.title: E-mails sent
panels.description: Failure e-mails the notifier sent in the selected time range (RF5; MailHog locally).

panels.title: Alerts firing
panels.description: Prometheus alerts firing now (rules in deploy/prometheus/rules; details in the table below and on the Prometheus /alerts page).

panels.title: Alerts (firing and pending)
panels.description: Every Prometheus alert that is pending (condition true, waiting for its 'for') or firing. There is no Alertmanager locally: this table and http://localhost:9091/alerts are where alerts show up.

panels.title: Request rate by route and status
panels.description: Requests per second served by the api, by route pattern and status (probes /healthz and /readyz left out). 5xx series are red.

panels.title: Uploads by result
panels.description: POST /api/v1/videos requests per 30 s that reached the handler, by result: accepted, or the error code of the rejection (unsupported_format, missing_file, payload_too_large, ...).

panels.title: 5xx ratio
panels.description: Share of api requests answered with a 5xx (probes left out). Dashed line: the 5% threshold of the APIHighErrorRatio alert.

panels.title: Latency p95 by route
panels.description: 95th percentile of the time to serve a request, per route pattern (histogram videoproc_http_request_duration_seconds). Uploads and downloads include the transfer, so they are slower than the JSON routes.

panels.title: Latency p50 / p95 / p99 ($route)
panels.description: Percentiles of the request duration over the routes picked in the 'route' variable at the top (All: every route but the probes).

panels.title: Jobs finished by outcome
panels.description: video.process deliveries handled per 30 s (per graph step on long ranges), by outcome: done (DONE), failed (bad content, FAILED), dead_lettered (given up, FAILED), retried (transient error, back through a retry queue), requeued, ignored.

panels.title: Job duration p50 / p95 (DONE)
panels.description: Time to process one video that ended DONE: download, ffmpeg, zip, upload of the zip and status change (videoproc_job_duration_seconds{outcome="done"}).

panels.title: Jobs in progress per worker
panels.description: Videos being processed by each worker replica (one series per container, found through Docker's DNS). Stacked: the height is the total parallelism (RF1). Scale with docker compose up -d --scale worker=N and a new series appears.

panels.title: Frames extracted
panels.description: Frames per second written to the zips of the videos that ended DONE (1 frame per second of video).

panels.title: Worker replicas up
panels.description: Worker containers Prometheus scrapes successfully (up == 1). Follows docker compose --scale worker=N within seconds.

panels.title: Queue video.process
panels.description: Messages in video.process (ready: waiting for a worker; unacked: being processed) and in its retry queues (delayed 2 s / 10 s / 30 s before the next attempt).

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: Consumers of the work queues: one per worker replica on video.process, one per notifier on video.notify. 0 on video.process fires NoWorkerConsumers.

panels.title: Outbox pending
panels.description: Rows waiting in the transactional outbox (ADR 0004) to be published to RabbitMQ. Normally 0 or close to it: the relays publish within about a second of an upload or status change.

panels.title: Notifications by result
panels.description: video.notify deliveries (video.failed events) handled per 30 s: sent (e-mail sent), duplicate (already notified), ignored, retried, dead_lettered (to video.notify.dlq), requeued.

panels.title: SMTP send duration p50 / p95
panels.description: Time to send one e-mail to the SMTP server (MailHog locally), successful sends.

panels.title: Queue video.notify
panels.description: Failure events waiting for the notifier (ready), being sent (unacked), delayed in the retry queues (10 s to 15 min) and given up in video.notify.dlq (red).

panels.title: List cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of GET /api/v1/videos answered from Redis (docs/cache.md). Every upload or status change of a user invalidates their pages, so the ratio drops while videos are being processed.

panels.title: List cache lookups by result
panels.description: Lookups of the list cache per second: hit, miss (read from Postgres, then cached), error (Redis failed, Postgres answered).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by each service instance (100% = one core), from process_cpu_seconds_total.

panels.title: Heap in use
panels.description: Go heap in use per service instance (go_memstats_heap_inuse_bytes). The worker's ffmpeg runs in a child process and is not included.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines per service instance. A steady climb without load points to a leak.
